meta.title: Write-Ahead Log: Durability Before the Data Page Is Flushed

segments.label: Normal write: log first, then acknowledge — the data page can be flushed later
Crash: the data page update never reached disk, but the WAL already has it
Recovery: replay the WAL to redo everything committed but not yet flushed

messages.label: flush dirty page — interrupted by crash
RECOVERY: replay log since last checkpoint

cards.title: Why Log Before Touching the Data
items: Appending to a sequential log is one fast, predictable disk operation — no seeking around a B-tree page
Updating the actual data page can be deferred and batched, off the write's critical path, without risking durability
The client's 'committed' only needs the log entry to be on disk, not the final page layout

cards.title: What Recovery Actually Does
items: On restart, the engine finds the last checkpoint and replays every WAL entry written after it
Any operation the log says was committed, but whose data page never made it to disk, gets re-applied
This is called redo recovery — it never has to ask the client to resend anything

cards.title: Where This Shows Up
items: PostgreSQL's WAL and MySQL/InnoDB's redo log
LSM-tree engines (RocksDB, Cassandra) still write a WAL before the write ever reaches the memtable
